title: Responses compatibility: tool-call routing and stream fidelity gap-catalog
creator: Maya Chen
description: Run a focused engineering audit and produce a prioritized gap catalog for feature parity between Redwood's Responses-compatible surface and OpenAI's Responses API. Focus areas: streaming event semantics, function/tool-call routing and confirmations, structured output enforcement, and edge-case behavior (partial deltas, aborts, provenance tokens). Deliverables: (1) gap catalog with severity and repro cases, (2) a compatibility shim design doc with trade-offs, (3) test harness and telemetry checks, (4) implementation plan for highest-risk gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Comprehensive gap catalog covering at least 20 distinct behavioral deltas with concrete reproduction steps
Design doc for a lightweight runtime shim that can transform OpenAI-style events to Redwood Responses semantics
Automated fuzz tests for streaming boundaries added to the responses-interop test suite
Telemetry dashboard that surfaces lossiness rates and tool routing mismatches per model and per region
repro_steps: 1) Use OpenAI Responses reference model to emit mixed tool-call and text streaming for a suite of prompts in /testdata/interop/. 2) Capture Redwood runtime events via stage-interop tracing hooks (trace-id). 3) Compare event sequences, field names (type/metadata), and deltas. 4) Record divergence examples (missing confirmation, truncated structured outputs, out-of-order tool-calls).
decisions: Prioritize non-lossy behavior for tool-calls and structured outputs over byte-for-byte parity of event names
Implement shim with an opt-in compatibility flag; default remains current Redwood Responses semantics to avoid regressions
Telemetry-backed gradual rollout: enable shim for 10% of test traffic, monitor lossiness and latency impact for 48h before expanding
tradeoffs_considered: Full semantic parity (heavy) vs lightweight normalization layer (favored): heavy parity requires deep changes to runtime buffering and ordering guarantees
Strict event ordering to match OpenAI can increase tail latency due to additional synchronization
Retaining Redwood structured-output enforcement reduces downstream ambiguity but may drop some OpenAI-specific metadata
risks: Customer breakage if shim accidentally drops function-call confirmation events
Increased tail latency for streaming responses leading to SLO breaches
False positives in lossiness telemetry leading to noisy alerts
mitigations: Run canary in isolated test workspace with synthetic traffic and selected customers
Add end-to-end contract tests covering interleaved tool-calls and partial deltas
Expose a debug header that captures original event payloads for postmortem analysis
work_done: Collected 34 divergence examples from internal fuzz runs (see /testdata/interop/2025-01-09-collect.json)
PoC shim implemented in runtime PR #7123 that normalizes 'tool.call' events and appends canonical confirmation markers
Telemetry instrumentation added (PR #184) to count 'missing_confirmation' and 'structured_parse_fail' events
notes: Observed common pattern: OpenAI emits a final 'tool_call' acknowledgement in a separate terminal event; Redwood currently expects a single consolidated tool call object. This leads to duplicate function invocations if left unmapped.
Some models stream JSON fragments for structured outputs; Redwood's strict JSON assembly step rejects partial fragments unless reassembled—introduces a window for parse failures.
Regional routing differences surface when fallback policies swap in a lightweight model variant that omits certain event fields (provenance/token IDs).
next_steps: Merge shim PoC behind feature flag and run staged canary (10% traffic) with telemetry gating
Author contract tests for interleaved streaming + tool-calls and add to CI
Prep customer communication template for early adopters in case behavior changes
Schedule cross-functional review with DX and Product to align on compatibility defaults
blockers: Need sign-off from runtime lead on acceptable tail-latency impact
Missing contract test harness for partial JSON fragment reassembly (tickets: ENG-905001)
